# Settings — Developers

Available on **All plans**.

## Deep links — where to find them

The Deep links block lives at **Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → Deep links** — this is the primary, canonical location. (A read-only summary also surfaces on the General settings page, but the block itself and any editing happen under **Developers**.) When a merchant asks "where are the deep links / where do I get the link", route them to **Settings → Developers**.

## Anchors (no setup needed)

- `#joy-home` — main widget home
- `#joy-ways-to-earn`
- `#joy-ways-to-redeem`
- `#joy-referral-program`

## Setup

**Shopify Admin → Online Store → Navigation → [Main menu / Footer] → Add menu item** → name (e.g., Rewards) + URL (paste `#joy-home`). Save → clicking that menu item opens the widget.

You can disable the floating widget button entirely once deeplinks are set up.

---

Available on **Advanced+**. Add/remove customer points by adding a Shopify tag.

## Enable

**Settings → Developers → Manage Tags** toggle on.

## Tag syntax

```
Joy: Add 500 - Place order #111 via POS
Joy: Subtract 100 - Refund
```

The number after Add/Subtract adjusts the balance; the comment tracks the reason.

Useful in **Shopify Flow** workflows that auto-tag customers with these strings — Joy reads tags and updates balances. Provides flexibility beyond the Joy API.

---

Use the official `joyso-hydrogen-sdk` npm package.

## Steps

1. **Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → Enable Custom Storefront development**
2. Install `joyso-hydrogen-sdk` in your Hydrogen project
3. In `app/root.jsx`: add the loader to fetch Joy data
4. Initialize Joy in root layout
5. Add CSP whitelist in `entry.server.jsx`
6. Optional CSS fix: Hydrogen quickstart uses `box-sizing: content-box` which can warp the floating button — add corrective CSS

Non-Plus stores can test with Storefront API key from a custom app in dev environment.

---

**Settings → Developers → Manage keys → Generate key** — creates App ID + Secret key.

**Important:** Generating a new key invalidates any previous key. If another app already uses the old credentials, you must update them.

---

## AI assistant access — manage loyalty via Claude & ChatGPT (Joy MCP)

Joy connects to AI assistants that support **MCP (Model Context Protocol) with remote + OAuth** — confirmed working with **Claude** and **ChatGPT**. Any other MCP-compatible AI assistant with the same remote+OAuth support should in theory also connect, but this isn't verified case-by-case — don't promise support for a specific third-party AI tool without checking first.

**Enable at:** Joy Admin → Settings → Developers → connect AI assistant. Full setup guide: `help.joy.so/settings/developers/connect-claude-and-chatgpt/`.

**What it's for:** a merchant who already works inside an AI assistant (with their own business context loaded) can ask it to pull loyalty data or make changes, instead of switching over to the Joy admin. Common use cases: a weekly/monthly loyalty summary, looking up or updating a specific customer's points/tier, or issuing a reward.

**Permission levels:**
- **Read-only** — the AI assistant can only view data (points, tiers, program info); it cannot make changes.
- **Full access** — the AI assistant can add/subtract points, change tiers, issue rewards, and adjust point balances. Any balance change shows a before/after preview before it's applied.

This is a new integration — scope may expand over time, so treat it as an evolving capability rather than a fixed, final feature list.

**Plan requirement (updated 2026-09):** connecting an AI assistant needs a **paid plan (Pro or higher)** — same gate as REST API v2 below, since every MCP tool call is executed as a REST API v2 request under the hood and draws from the same per-shop quota. Free/Starter cannot connect at all (the consent screen shows an upgrade error). See **REST API v2 & MCP access by plan** below for the exact numbers.

## REST API v2 & MCP access by plan

**Updated 2026-09-10 — REST API v2, Webhook API, and MCP are no longer Ultimate-exclusive.** They are a **paid-plan entitlement**: any paid plan (Pro and above) has access, and plans differ only by **rate** (burst limit + daily quota), not by on/off. This replaces the earlier "Ultimate only" policy that applied from 2025-09-17 through early September 2026.

- **Free / Starter** — **no access**. A call returns **HTTP 402 Payment Required** (`error: "plan_upgrade_required"`), not 403 — the response includes an `upgrade_url` pointing straight to the shop's subscription page. If a merchant reports a `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`/402 error, that means they're on Free/Starter; the fix is upgrading, not a bug.
- **Pro** — access. **30 requests / 10 seconds** burst, **200 requests/day** quota. Sized as a setup/configuration budget (enough to stand the loyalty program up and reconfigure it via API or an AI assistant), not for continuous/production traffic.
- **Advanced** — access. **60 requests / 10 seconds** burst, **2,000 requests/day** quota. Setup budget plus room for a light ongoing integration.
- **Ultimate (Enterprise)** — **unlimited**, no daily quota. This is the plan for sustained production traffic — anything that scales with the merchant's own shoppers rather than with the merchant's own usage.

**MCP shares one counter with direct API traffic** — there is no separate MCP limit. A single AI-assistant session (e.g. "set up my loyalty program") can spend a meaningful slice of a Pro/Advanced shop's daily quota, since each tool call the assistant makes is one API request.

Hitting the **daily quota** (not the plan gate) returns **429 Too Many Requests** with a `Retry-After` header and resets at the next UTC midnight — this is normal usage hitting a real ceiling, not an error, and the merchant's own upgrade path (a higher tier) is the fix if it happens often.

## What's included with paid-plan API access

- **REST API v2** (and v1) — manage customers, point transactions, rewards, VIP tiers, referrals
- **Webhook API** — real-time notifications for 20+ loyalty events (points earned, tier upgraded, coupon used, etc.)
- **Headless / Hydrogen** support
- Cursor-based pagination, comprehensive error handling, automatic data filtering

## Authentication

Credentials are found in **Settings → Developers → Manage keys → Generate key** (App ID + Secret Key). The **Manage keys** panel also shows a badge with the shop's current rate limit (e.g. "200 API requests/day", "Unlimited API requests", or "Not included on your plan" for Free/Starter).

Official docs: `devdocs.joy.so/joy-rest-api-v2/rest-api-v2`

## Upgrade path

**Settings → Subscription → All Plans** to upgrade — Pro is enough to unlock REST API v2 / MCP access; Advanced adds headroom for a light integration; Ultimate removes the daily quota entirely for production/continuous traffic.

# Checkout Page Integration

**Shopify Plus only** — Checkout extensibility is a Shopify platform restriction, not Joy's. Most checkout blocks need **Ultimate** plan + Checkout Extensibility.

## Available blocks

| Block | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Quick Redeem** | One-click redemption of currently-affordable rewards (recommend 2-4 max) |
| **Available Rewards** | Lists rewards customer can redeem with current point balance |
| **All Discounts** | Comprehensive grid of all discount rewards (locked + unlocked) |
| **Coupon list at checkout** | Shows previously-redeemed unused coupons inline |
| **Redeem at checkout page** | Convert points → discount directly at checkout |
| **Referral at Checkout** | Lets customer enter referral link/code to claim referral reward |

All add via **Joy Admin → On-site content → Checkout page → [block] → Edit in Theme Editor → Add Block**.

---

Streamlined Shopify UI extension that shows only **affordable** rewards. Ultimate + Checkout Extensibility.

## Best practices

- Show 2-4 rewards max to keep it "quick"
- Set priority by value, popularity, customer behavior, or manual ordering
- Customer redeems → points convert to temporary discount; cancel = points refunded instantly
- Enable on each redeem program: **Reward programs → Redeem programs → [program] → Redeem at checkout page** toggle

---

Customer enters referral link or code at checkout to instantly claim the referral reward.

## Setup

**Joy App → On-site content → Checkout page → Referral at Checkout → Edit in Theme Editor** → drag block, edit text:
- Title: "Have a referral link?"
- Description: "Enter your referral link or code below to claim your {{ referral_reward }} discount."

Cart Drawer support coming soon.

## Points earned + balance in the order confirmation email

The **Joy Point Calculator** block, placed in the **checkout order summary** via Shopify's **Checkout and accounts editor**, writes order attributes that a merchant can then surface on Shopify's own **Order confirmation** notification with a Liquid snippet — so the customer sees their loyalty points right in the confirmation email, not just on-screen at checkout.

**Requirement:** the block must be placed in the checkout order summary via the Checkout and accounts editor, which Shopify only makes available on **Shopify Plus**. If the block can't be placed (non-Plus store), the feature simply produces nothing — no error, no broken email.

The block can write up to **three** order attributes, all controlled by the single **"Show points earned in order confirmation email"** setting:

| Attribute | Value | Present when |
|---|---|---|
| `Joy loyalty points earned` | Estimated points for this order (a display estimate, not a guarantee of the amount actually awarded) | The estimate is a positive number |
| `Joy loyalty points balance` | The customer's point balance **at checkout time** (does not include this order's points) | The buyer matches an existing Joy member |
| `Joy loyalty points label` | The merchant's **Custom point label** (singular/plural, matching the on-screen banner) | Either number above is present |

The merchant pastes a Liquid snippet (provided in the setting's UI) into the Order confirmation email template to render these — e.g. "You're set to earn {{ points }} {{ label }} from this order" and "Your current balance: {{ balance }} {{ label }}." Changing the **Custom point label** applies to orders placed afterwards only; already-placed orders keep the label that was current when they were placed.

# Referral Program

Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Referrals**. Basic features on All plans; advanced (Shopify customer/order tagging) on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

## Reward types

| For | Available reward types |
|---|---|
| **Referee** (new customer) | Points, Store credit, Discount %, Discount amount |
| **Referrer** | Points, **Points (based on order value)**, Store credit (fixed), Store credit (% of referee order), Discount %, Discount amount |

**Points based on order value (added 2026-08-10):** set at **Reward method → Points based on order value**. Merchant enters a points-per-$1 rate applied to the referee's order **subtotal after discount** (shipping and tax excluded) and chooses a rounding rule; a preview shows an example calculation. This exists so a merchant running a points-based loyalty program can reward referrers proportionally without granting Store Credit permissions they may not want to give.

- **Tier-based rewards** — Customize referrer reward by VIP tier. For the points-based-on-order-value method, turning this on switches the setup screen from a single preview number to a reminder to set a rate for each tier individually.
- **Max amount cap on % discount** — e.g., "15% off, up to $30" — set independently per side, off by default
- The configured rate shows to customers on the Referral block of **Widget V4**, e.g. *"2 points per $1 your friend spends."*

## Referral redirection URL

Default = homepage. Change to any landing page (e.g., a campaign page).

## Sharing channels

Customers share their unique link via the loyalty widget across selected social/email channels. Email invite (see next chunk) is built-in.

---

## Flow

1. Referrer shares their unique link
2. Referee clicks link → lands on referral page → enters email to claim → **7-day cookie** stored on device → activity = pending. The **referee's** reward (coupon / store credit) is issued at this claim step; the **referrer's** reward stays pending until the referee actually orders.
3. Referee places order with the **same email** → activity = complete on thank-you page → both rewarded.

**When the referrer's reward is granted** — the referrer is rewarded only after the referee places a qualifying order, following the shop's earn-status setting (same as points earning):

- **Reward on Paid** (default, `earnByOrderStatus = financial_status`): granted as soon as the referee's order is **Paid**.
- **Reward on Fulfilled / Partial**: the reward waits until the order reaches that fulfilment status. While the order is Paid but not yet fulfilled, the referral shows **"Awaiting fulfilment"** (this is normal — it means the order was placed and is waiting to fulfil, not that something failed).

## Troubleshooting (referrer didn't get reward)

- **Different emails** — referee used different email at claim vs checkout. Both sides need same email
- **App pixel disabled** — check **Shopify Admin → Settings → Customer Events → Joy** is enabled. Toggle program off/on to re-sync
- Cookie expired (>7 days between click and purchase)

## Common false negatives when testing

- **"Running in test mode" message** means the referral program is in **Sandbox / preview** — go live for real rewards to be issued.
- **Same PC / same browser:** on a device where the merchant is logged into their own store, the referral page may show only the code without prompting for a friend's email. Test in incognito, another account, or a phone to see the real behaviour.

## Anti-cheat

Built-in fraud prevention stops customers gaming the program with multiple accounts. Configure limits per program in the referral settings. When anti-cheat is enabled, a referral is blocked when the referrer and referee share the **same browser, same email, or same IP address**, or reuse the **same order**. The referee's order must also have a **subtotal greater than $0** — a $0 order does not qualify the referrer for a reward.

## Referral limits

- **Referral limit per customer** (field label in **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Referrals → referral settings**) — caps the number of successful referrals a single referrer can earn from. Example: set to 5 to let each member earn rewards from a maximum of 5 successful referrals; combine with a fixed per-referral reward (e.g. store credit or points equivalent to a fixed amount) to naturally cap the total a member can earn.
- **Plan-based limit** — the **Free plan** caps how many referral orders can be rewarded. To lift the cap, the merchant upgrades to a paid plan. Higher plans raise or remove this limit.

## Reward revocation on refund

If the referee's qualifying order is **fully refunded**, the referrer's reward is **automatically revoked** when the merchant has enabled **Auto-revoke referrer reward** on the referral program (points are deducted back and a revoke activity is logged). If the setting is off, the referrer keeps the reward even after a refund.

---

Available on **All plans**. Referrer enters friend's email in the widget → system auto-sends a branded invitation email containing the referrer's name, the discount/reward, and the referral link.

Delivery channels supported:
- Joy's built-in email
- Klaviyo
- Shopify Flow

The invite email goes to the **referee** (carrying the referrer's unique link), not to the referrer. Settings live at **Joy Admin → Settings → Notifications** for the built-in template; for automation, configure at **Referral program → Referral flow → Automated email sharing**. To build this in **Klaviyo**, choose the Klaviyo trigger **"Joy: Referral Link Sent"** and build the flow around it.

**Prefix gotcha:** `Joy: ` is the default event-name prefix. Shops that connected **Klaviyo between 2025-10-08 and 2026-03-05** were backfilled with prefix `Klaviyo Joy: ` instead — for those shops the trigger is named `Klaviyo Joy: Referral Link Sent`, not `Joy: Referral Link Sent`. The Joy Admin UI always previews the `Joy: ` form regardless of which prefix a shop actually has, so if the trigger isn't firing, check when Klaviyo was connected and have the merchant look for both name variants in Klaviyo's metric list (see kb_integrations-email).

Two related Klaviyo/Omnisend events for the rest of the referral flow: `Joy: Referral Friend Complete` (fires when the referred friend completes their first qualifying purchase) and `Joy: Referee Claim Reward` (fires when the friend claims their reward).

**`Joy: Referee Claim Reward` — event property names (confirmed working since the 2026-09-08 fix):** the `customer` on this event is already the **referee** (the one claiming), so the useful new field is `Referrer email` — the person who referred them. The event carries exactly three custom properties: `Referrer email`, `Reward type` (`coupon` or store-credit), and `Reward` (the actual coupon code for a coupon reward, or the store-credit amount for a store-credit reward — same field name, two possible content shapes depending on `Reward type`).

**Before 2026-09-08, real sends of this event carried NONE of these properties** — only the "Send test" preview in Klaviyo's trigger picker (Admin → Integration → Klaviyo → step 3) had fixture values, which is why the test preview looked right while real events differed. If a merchant's Klaviyo flow references a coupon-code variable name that doesn't match `Reward` above, the flow was likely built against an older real event (pre-fix, no fields at all) or copied a guessed name from an earlier support reply — have them rebuild the flow's filter/personalization against `Referrer email` / `Reward type` / `Reward`.

When the friend purchases, both sides get rewards + confirmation emails.

## Merchant referral program (refer-a-merchant)

This is a **separate program from the customer referral program above** — here the merchant refers other Shopify merchants to Joy, not customers referring friends.

- **Set up:** No setup needed by the merchant. Eligible merchants see a banner "Referral Program" on the **Homepage** or **Settings → Subscription** page, and get a unique referral code/link to share with other Shopify merchants.
- **Eligibility:** Banner + program only shows to merchants who meet eligibility requirements (see Joy's merchant referral program guide for the current criteria).
- **Reward (referrer merchant) — Joy credit toward their next billing cycle**, tiered by the referrer's plan: **$29** on Essential, **$90** on Advanced, **$250** on Ultimate, per successful referral.
- **Reward (referred merchant):** discount off their first 3 months — 50% on Essential, 30% on Advanced, 20% on Ultimate.
- **Milestone bonus** (Advanced + Ultimate referrers only): extra **+$30** at 2 referrals, **+$100** at 5 referrals, **+$300** at 10 referrals.
- **Why it exists:** Joy's paid-ads/CAC channel for acquiring merchants was costly and underperforming, so merchant-to-merchant referral was added as a cheaper acquisition channel (added 2026-05-25).

## Referral export — Status detail column

Merchants export referral activity from the **Customers → Activities** export modal (same export used for points activity — see kb_analytics), ticking the columns they want, including **Status** and **Completed At**.

- **Status** keeps emitting the **raw** internal value — `pending_referral`, `complete_referral`, etc. — unchanged, so merchant scripts and spreadsheet formulas that already key off it keep working.
- A new, additive **Status detail** column carries the human-readable state instead: **Pending**, **Awaiting fulfillment**, **Completed**, or **Cancel**. It's included automatically whenever the merchant ticks the **Status** checkbox — there's no separate checkbox to turn it on, and it's emitted right after the Status column.
- **Completed At** is populated **only** for rows where the referral has actually completed (`Status` = Completed) — it's left blank for Pending, Awaiting fulfillment, and Cancel rows, since those haven't completed yet. If a merchant previously saw a filled-in Completed At on a non-completed row, that was the old (incorrect) behavior; it now correctly reflects only real completions.

## Referral activity in the widget (Widget V4)

The referral block in **Widget V4** shows the referrer their own referral activity directly, without needing a CS lookup or the admin export: **Invited**, **Completed**, and **Pending** counts, plus a list of individual referral activity entries. This gives a customer self-serve visibility into whether their friends' invites have converted, matching the same Pending / Awaiting fulfillment / Completed states used in the admin export (see **Referral export — Status detail column** above).
